messages:
Mike H: Quick sync — proposing we move from per-tenant long-lived private endpoints to a delegated "private-net shard" model: a small number of ephemeral, managed shards per region/az that handle control-plane egress for many tenants. Goal: reduce ENI count, smoother IP usage, simpler peering topology. Tradeoffs: mapping tenant->shard, preserving customer source IP for those who require it, cert/mtls handoff, and graceful cutover. Thoughts?

Elaine: Interesting. Reduces endpoint sprawl for sure. Two immediate q's: 1) how do we preserve src IP for customers that rely on it? 2) what are failure/fallback semantics if a shard loses capacity? :thinking_face: 

Raj P: For srcIP we can either: a) keep SNAT and add an authenticated header (X-Redwood-Src) or b) offer an opt-in passthrough mode using per-tenant ENI or ENI-pinning. Some partners cannot accept header spoofing, so (b) still needed. Fallback: route to a secondary shard or fall back to per-tenant ENI if shard is out-of-capacity.

Sara L: Ops notes — per-tenant ENI fallback means we still need to support the old model; rollout has to be gradual. Suggest canary on non-regulated tenants first and telemetry to detect policy violations. Also: who owns shard autoscaling? infra team?

infra-bot: deploy-bot: created draft rfc: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/privatenet-shards (DRAFT) — assigned to @Mike_H and @Elaine.

Mike H: Quick sketch of mapping config (pseudo-terraform):
```hcl
resource "redwood_shard" "shard" {
  region = "us-west-2"
  az     = "us-west-2a"
  nat_pool = ["10.10.0.0/24"]
  preserve_srcip = false # default, opt-in per-tenant
}
resource "redwood_tenant_attachment" "attach" {
  tenant_id = "acct-123"
  shard_id  = redwood_shard.shard.id
  mode      = "delegated" # | passthrough
}
```

Elaine: Nice. Observability we need: per-tenant path choice counters, SRCIP-preserved-percent, per-shard connection errors, and shard-eviction/reassign events. TTLs for mapping need thinking — too short causes churn, too long prevents redistrib.

Raj P: IPv6: customers will want v6 preserved. Two approaches: 1) have dual-stack shards that maintain v6 pools, 2) prefer v6 passthrough when tenant asks. Both increase address management complexity. Also callout: some partner firewalls match on L4 tuples — our NAT semantics must remain stable.

Sara L: Rollout proposal:
- Phase 0: design doc + sig-off (2w)
- Phase 1: implement shard control-plane + telemetry, test in sandbox (3w)
- Phase 2: canary with 5 low-risk tenants, no srcip preservation (4w)
- Phase 3: opt-in srcip passthrough for selected tenants + docs (4w)
- Phase 4: wider migration + automatic reassignment (ongoing)
Add runbooks for shard eviction and manual failback.

Mike H: Agreed. Action items: 1) I'll flesh the RFC with failure/fallback semantics and per-tenant policy flags. 2) @Elaine will spec observability metrics and alerts. 3) @Raj P to prototype passthrough flow and NAT semantics. 4) @Sara L to author cutover runbook and canary checklist. Meeting to sync next Wednesday 9am PT.

Elaine: I'll add a draft metrics dashboard and a short alerting playbook (SLO: shard error rate < 0.5% over 5m).

Raj P: Will spike the passthrough proof-of-concept — focus on connection preservation and cert handoff.

Mike H: Thanks all. Keeping the RFC light on text and heavy on failure diagrams helped yesterday in the design review — will include sequence diagrams. :thumbsup:
